note: Two roots per toast page, each its own census page, both sides for both themes, on the mirror (http://localhost:4184/geist/toast) and the docs census page (http://localhost:4180/census/toast). The page's own ten showcases render a button only (no root on either side); the sixteen sketched examples that follow them (tools/geist/sketch/toast.*.json) render the client-only states on the mirror, and on ours a viewport per example on a queue of its own (the example script sets it), filled by the `prepare` script of the toast run: it pushes the same messages, expands the stack of the Stack expanded example with a mouseenter on the area, and puts the Entering and Leaving toasts into their phases; it waits on the elements' updates only (no timers). toast: the toast box (marker data-geist-toast; ours acme-toast >> .toast under acme-toaster, every toast with `each`), with its column, visual, message row, the assistive-tech type span, the text, the controls (undo, close), the action row (cancel, action) and the ::after bridge; the cancel button's width follows its label, so it reads as soft. toast-area: the viewport (div.toast-area; ours .area). Run the toast run of both themes before the area runs, or reload the mirror between: the area run's own state passes set and clear data-hover on the area, and the Stack expanded sketch carries that attribute as its state (census.js keeps a pre-existing state attribute, but the mirror must be fully loaded before the first run so its sheets are rewritten). Run the reference side only after the page has loaded: a run right after navigation finds the sheets empty. toast-mobile: the toast run again with both panes at the mobile preset (375 by 812): the reference's `max-sm` breakpoint (400px and under) hides the third toast of a stack and the box shrinks to the viewport less two gaps (327px); the one-sentence text wraps in our font there and not in the reference's, so the text's height and the boxes that follow it read as soft, and (hover: hover) is false in the emulation on both sides.
